**Finding submitted — deviation (critical, ip-data).**

**What the document does:** Article III (p0048) vests *all* right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and its Intellectual Property Rights in Licensor. Because "DERIVATIVE WORK" (§1.3, p0005) is defined as any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements based on the Licensed Technology, and Article VII(b) (p0087) contemplates that we pay Licensor for "further development and customization work for creating a unique client front end," we would fund bespoke development and own none of it — receiving only the narrow, terminable Field-of-Use licence in Article II (p0030, p0043). There is also no provision anywhere reserving our rights in our own trading, order, client and account data; the "Confidential Information" and "Intellectual Property Rights" definitions run one way, in Licensor's favour only.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** a single inserted paragraph after Article III that (a) confirms we retain all rights in Licensee Data and that Licensor may use it only to perform the Agreement, (b) assigns to us the customization deliverables we pay for, with Licensor keeping its pre-existing platform IP and granting a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to any of that IP embedded in the deliverables, and (c) rules out joint ownership. Licensor's ownership of the Platform itself is untouched, which is acceptable under the playbook.

**Fallback offered in the comment:** Licensor may own the customization deliverables provided we get a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense them for our business.
